newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks stumble at open, banks dip.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks stumble at open, banks dip.

text.p: The Australian share market stumbled at the open on Wednesday after the Dow's climb slowed amid concerns over U.S. interest rates.
The All Ordinaries index lost 8.8 points to 2,459.5.
Brokers said losses were mostly modest with the big banks dipping initially before finding support at their early lows while the resources leaders started mixed.
"It's a bit on the quiet side with not much of a lead from overseas," said dealer Phillip Toop of Brisbane-based brokerage, Lance Jones.
"The market is a bit of a mixed bag with a few up and a few down but nothing really major."
Results continued with upmarket retailer David Jones posting a 50 percent lower first half net profit of A$22.34 million (US$17.78 million). Its shares were four cents lower at A$1.70.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to four, while about 45 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
